GOAL_OBJECTIVE
GOAL: Develop and rigorously evaluate a Kazinnik-anchored RBI MPC research contribution.

OBJECTIVE AND SCOPE

Develop the strongest feasible, scientifically valid RBI MPC adaptation of Kazinnik and Sinclair’s FOMC In Silico, and independently evaluate one consequential contribution beyond transferring the framework to India. Aim for the methodological standards of a leading journal. Deliver an improved reproducible research package and an honest evidence assessment; journal acceptance and favorable AI opinions are not completion conditions.

Work in the existing AI_project repository on project_upgrade_codex. Preserve main, existing work, original sources, results, transcripts, checkpoints, reviews and negative findings. Inspect applicable instructions and current implementation before editing. Manuscript checking, editing and journal formatting are outside this goal.

Begin from the existing bounded readiness assessment. Reuse verified work, reconcile partial components and preserve prior ledgers. Do not restart the project or repeat a test solely to demonstrate activity.

BOUNDS FOR THIS NEW RUN

These allowances start only when this goal is activated. Earlier work remains inherited evidence and retains its historical accounting.

• At most three substantive repair cycles.
• At most two scientific reviewer dispatches: one final critique and one documented infrastructure/isolation retry. Reuse existing diagnostics; no new initial publication review.
• At most eight elapsed hours from activation, including parallel workers and tool/provider waits, excluding explicit user pauses. Reserve the last hour for closeout.
• Use only the remaining existing provider spending allowance. Do not increase caps, purchase resources or silently substitute models.

Maintain one run ID and cumulative ledger. Failed, interrupted and contaminated attempts consume the appropriate allowances. All workers share the bounds. Resumptions, renamed studies, revised plans and newly discovered findings never reset this run’s counters.

A repair cycle comprises a stated blocker or hypothesis, one bounded repair/evaluation batch, and an evidence-table update. It cannot contain an open-ended nested improvement loop.

Before each batch, declare numeric experiment, call, retry, cost and runtime limits within the remaining allowance. Do not begin work that cannot fit the remaining budget and closeout reserve.

1. ESTABLISH VERSION-SPECIFIC REFERENCE FIDELITY

Use these primary reference locations:

https://www2.gwu.edu/~forcpgm/2025-005.pdf
https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5424097

Identify the exact full-text version inspected, its date, source and SHA-256. Inspect the available August 2025 draft and attempt to obtain a later full revision within a declared, bounded acquisition allowance.

Keep revised-abstract statements separate from verified full-text methods. Missing revised methods or materials remain explicit limitations. Do not invent them, merge incompatible versions, or let retrieval block all work on an available version.

Create a paper-to-project matrix containing:
paper section/equation or protocol; implemented behavior; code/data reference; faithful adaptation, justified departure, unsupported assertion or missing component; decisive verification evidence.

Cover personas, real-time information, initial beliefs, deliberation, numerical comparator, voting/aggregation, scenarios, validation and inference. Verify the selected mechanisms needed for the RBI adaptation, with computational reproduction where materials permit. Do not transfer the paper’s reported performance or credibility to this implementation.

The existing Taylor-rule/Monte Carlo track must not be described as the paper’s generalized Bayesian voting implementation. Either implement and verify the relevant reference mechanism where scientifically necessary and feasible, or justify the Taylor/reaction-function track as a distinct mechanical comparator.

Any dual-track interpretation must address differences in initial beliefs, information, actions, aggregation, targets and resources. Unexplained differences cannot be attributed to behavioral departures from rationality.

2. FREEZE ONE MEANINGFUL INCREMENTAL QUESTION

Choose and justify one primary scientific question using calibration/development evidence before new evaluation. Explain what it adds beyond geography and additional engineering.

Institutional rules, information visibility or persona/deliberation mechanisms may motivate the question, but their importance and identification must be argued.

Treat these outcomes separately:

• Forecasting: exact rate, basis-point error, hike/cut/hold and committee stance.
• Dissent: exact-rate disagreement and formal stance dissent, separately from literal ballots, reservations and guidance disagreement.
• Consensus: predeclared ballot agreement and preference dispersion across rounds. Distinguish the proposed mechanism from copying the chair, aggregation or coercive instructions.

Deliberation need not improve forecasts to yield an informative result. More consensus does not establish better policy or real-world institutional benefit. Positive, null and negative findings are acceptable. An imprecise estimate is not proof of no effect or equivalence.

Freeze the primary claim, estimand, endpoints, cohort/eligibility, missing-history/label policy, source vintages and cutoffs, personas, models, prompts, comparators, resource matching, sampling, failure rules and statistical analysis.

Declare already exposed outcomes; existing historical panels remain retrospective. Scientific changes after new outcome inspection become separately identified exploratory analyses and cannot replace the frozen primary analysis to obtain a win.

3. REPAIR DECISIVE BLOCKERS AND RUN THE STUDY

Prioritize validated inputs, integration and decisive evidence over optional engineering polish. Integrate existing rolling-persona, roster/stance, comparator and output-gap components only where needed by the frozen question.

Obtain defensible source availability, pre-cutoff membership and supported outcome semantics. Missing values remain missing. Unavailable inputs and unsupported meetings follow the frozen eligibility policy.

Use meaningful hold/persistence and calibration-selected baselines. Select the smallest controls sufficient to identify the primary mechanism. Consider full versus independent agents, joint-persona versus macro-only, and relevant persona-shuffle/no-score, authority, order or visibility controls. Avoid experiments without a scientific purpose.

Align meetings, information, targets and institutional resolution rules. Match resources or explicitly quantify their differences.

Include informative policy regimes/transitions for predictive claims. Repeating the eight all-hold meetings cannot establish useful general forecasting.

Actual live-model execution is required where the claim depends on model behavior. Mock fixtures, arithmetic checks, cache replay and metadata lookups are supporting engineering evidence only.

Preserve frozen request identity, raw generations, model/settings metadata, calls/tokens/cost, environment, hashes and every failure under immutable experiment/condition/replicate identities.

Budget, cancellation and provenance failures propagate. No silent fallback, repeated prompting until success or model substitution. Cache replay remains labeled replay.

Use meeting-level paired comparisons and justified temporal uncertainty. Account for sample adequacy, stochastic replication, missing-target sensitivity and multiple comparisons. Calls, members, rounds and Monte Carlo draws do not create additional independent meetings.

Independently recompute central results from raw outputs and verify the integrated source-to-result path.

Simulator interventions support simulator-local effects. Stronger causal, cognition, equilibrium or welfare claims require corresponding evidence.

4. ASSESS FIXED CRITERIA AND OBTAIN ONE FINAL CRITIQUE

Maintain a PASS / FAIL / UNVERIFIED evidence table for:

A. Reference fidelity and justified departures.
B. Important incremental contribution relative to verified prior work.
C. Source, timing, persona and label validity.
D. Identification, meaningful baselines and actual empirical execution.
E. Measurement, uncertainty and absence of pseudoreplication.
F. Integrated reproducibility, provenance and failure transparency.
G. Conclusions proportional to evidence.

Specify each criterion’s acceptance evidence before evaluation and cite the actual final artifacts. Missing evidence cannot pass. Do not lower criteria or substitute a trivial question to finish.

Give the final reviewer only a neutral contract, workings, scientific file map and frozen current implementation/inputs/protocol/raw evidence, including negative findings.

Exclude parent chat, memory, previous reviews, remediation plans and Git history. Verify injected context and record actual access restrictions; a fresh agent name is insufficient.

If context or access contamination prevents independence, preserve the attempt, count its dispatch and label its findings non-independent. Do not present that critique as independent validation.

Require independent source checks, central recomputation where feasible, evidence-linked criterion judgments, critical versus optional findings and review limitations.

The reviewer evaluates one immutable version. An infrastructure/isolation retry must preserve the scientific specification and attempt record and remain within the two-dispatch allowance. A negative scientific verdict does not authorize an approval-seeking retry.

AI critique supplies criticism, not journal certification. Preserve disagreements and adjudicate them using evidence. New objections enter the final gap report; they do not reopen the repair loop. Subsequent changes must be labeled unreviewed.

5. STOP, DELIVER AND DISTINGUISH THE OUTCOMES

Stop substantive work when:

• All criteria are supported with no unresolved critical flaw;
• Any allowance is exhausted;
• A necessary dependency is unavailable within the remaining allowance; or
• Two successive repair cycles yield no substantive scientific progress.

Deliver the versioned paper-to-project matrix, frozen protocol, reproducible package, criterion evidence table, raw evidence and run ledger.

The final report must contain changes and rationale, checks actually run, effect estimates and uncertainty, nulls/failures/contrary findings, exact remaining gaps, reproduction commands, artifact paths and the smallest next actions.

If stopped before a study can run, retain completed phases and mark later phases missing or blocked. Do not fabricate artifacts or claim their completion.

At minimum, deliver the acquired-source/version record, inspected-method matrix, evidence/gap assessment and accounting needed to justify the stop.

End with one status:

1. EVIDENCE SUPPORTS A SCIENTIFICALLY DEFENSIBLE RBI ADAPTATION AND THE DECLARED CONTRIBUTION WITHIN THE TESTED SCOPE.
All mandatory criteria are supported. This is not journal acceptance.

2. RESEARCH INCOMPLETE — SPECIFIED EVIDENCE OR RESOURCES REMAIN NECESSARY.
Identify the exact unmet criteria.

3. CURRENT EVIDENCE DOES NOT SUPPORT THE DECLARED CONTRIBUTION.
Specify which claims failed and how far the evidence generalizes.

All three statuses can complete this bounded task once the required completed-phase artifacts and honest remaining-gap report are delivered and verified.

State separately whether the adaptation, contribution and publication readiness were established. Budget exhaustion alone does not complete an undelivered assessment.

Stop after delivery. Further research or review requires a new user instruction. Never continue until an AI reviewer says “elite research grade.”
